parole.testo: Borrowed from Hebrew כְּתִיבָה (kăṯiḇá, “writing”) via Yiddish כּתיבֿה (ksive), from Hebrew כָּתַב (kaṯáḇ, “write”).
From Hebrew מְזוּזָה (m'zuzá), via Yiddish מזוזה (mezuze).
Borrowed from Hebrew חלה (khalá), probably by way of Yiddish חלה (khale).

parole.testo: From Hebrew שְׁמוֹנֶה (shmone, “eight”), referring to 8:00 a.m. when the cells were searched each morning in the Odessa prison prior to the communist revolution. Gračov does not give an etymology. Krysin claims a Yiddish origin, without quoting the Yiddish form. Elistratov compares with dialectal шм
